runners_data.name: C Pas Possible
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with one piece of useful form — third at 3m on Good going — and Andrew Kinirons sends him here 52 days fresh; the step back in trip from that effort is a mild query but the going suits and he can race prominently with an unknown ceiling.

runners_data.name: Dad Sez
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott which is an obvious booking upgrade, but this horse ran U last time and his style and going preference are genuinely unknown; treat with caution despite the stable's 14-day strike rate of 3/35.

runners_data.name: De Jour En Jour
runners_data.note: A consistent placer on Good and Heavier ground — three seconds and a third from six attempts — who races prominently and handles this trip well; Keith Donoghue knows the horse, headgear noted, but the win has eluded him and he may fill a place again rather than go one better.

runners_data.name: Eternal Reward
runners_data.note: Long absence of 297 days is the headline concern for Danny Mullins and Margaret Mullins; raced over shorter trips previously and carries a "fades in finish" flag that makes this 2m6f test on the comeback look demanding — likely needs the run.

runners_data.name: Excessivebehaviour
runners_data.note: 248 days off the track for Mark Walsh and Martin Brassil, and the "fades in finish" tendency combined with a solo turf run over 2m2f makes this trip a genuine stamina ask on return; difficult to trust at any price without a fitness run under his belt.

runners_data.name: Frankie's Freebie
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton on a 23-day turnaround for his father's yard — consistent form figures of 240-22 on Good ground over similar distances; amateur rider on a horse who places freely but has not won yet, likely to press for a prominent position but may lack the finishing kick.

runners_data.name: I Can Find Em
runners_data.note: Gary McGill's five-year-old was placed twice before a blank run and hasn't been seen for 116 days; the style and going suitability are marked unknown, and the amateur rider Mr O McGill riding for the family yard adds a wildcard element in a big field.

runners_data.name: Jeroboam Machin
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race — Emmet Mullins sends him here 19 days after his last run with Good-ground form — but the STYLE_FIT tag warns he is racing away from his natural role at this trip and in this field; his best form came over shorter distances on Soft and he may not see out 2m6f on Good.

runners_data.name: Killowen House
runners_data.note: Paul John Gilligan's six-year-old has three runs on Good going at similar trips and placed twice; his true racing style is hold-up, so in a 21-runner field he is likely to find himself closer to midfield than ideal — a genuine closing run from the back is compromised by field size.

runners_data.name: Kiltinan
runners_data.note: 241 days off and only one run to his name — fourth over 2m on Good — for Michael McDonagh; the unknown style and going preference make him very difficult to assess, and the long layoff means fitness is a reasonable concern.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney's seven-year-old has a patchy record including a fall and multiple placed efforts around 2m-3m on Good; a 19-day turnaround and the turf headgear noted, but finishing positions have been mid-to-rear and a maiden win has not come despite multiple opportunities.

runners_data.name: Mr Erwitt
runners_data.note: Very poor form figures including pulled-ups across six starts for V T O'Brien, and he fades in the finish — his natural style is hold-up but the field size means he races in midfield rather than off the back; the STYLE_FIT and "fades" tags together make him a very difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Mr Hollywood
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends in a six-year-old with just one run — a third over 2m2f on Good — but that horse showed class-level form for the yard and Brian Hayes is a strong booking; races as a hold-up type with a habit of placing, and the Galway straight suits a horse conserving energy for a late challenge.

runners_data.name: Ol Parson
runners_data.note: Has form figures of P, 2, 4, 9 and 6 across varied ground, with his best effort a second on Soft; six-year-old debut over fences aside, the Good-ground form is uninspiring and the amateur rider Conor Clarke reduces confidence in a competitive 21-runner field.

runners_data.name: Rumi Rock
runners_data.note: Only 8 days since last run which is an unusually short turnaround — Edward Power's five-year-old has two runs on Good at 18f and 20f both resulting in unplaced finishes; races hold-up and fades, which in a sustainably-paced race makes a winning performance hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Tom Mac
runners_data.note: Lightly raced six-year-old, 114 days off, with one run — sixth over 2m7f on Good — for Paul O'Flynn; Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride which is the most notable positive, but the form is thin and the unknown style ceiling makes him speculative.

runners_data.name: Trotters Traders
runners_data.note: Paul John Gilligan's five-year-old ran 16th on his sole start over just 17f on Good, carrying a "fades in finish" flag; nothing in the form to suggest he can reverse that trend stepping up dramatically in trip and class here.

runners_data.name: Trev The Rev
runners_data.note: A four-year-old making just his second start for Paul John Gilligan — pulled up on Soft ground last time and 120 days ago — and his style is unknown; the lightest weight in the race at 161lbs helps marginally but the experience deficit in a 21-runner field is a serious concern.

runners_data.name: Al Arrivee
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins/Patrick Mullins combination carries maximum confidence — two wins from five starts on Good, form of /124-1 showing he nearly always places; 52 days fresh but the stable's 14-day strike rate of 5/26 is strong and his proximity to the lead in a controlled race makes him the most dangerous prominent racer here.

runners_data.name: Shoda
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's five-year-old has one win but that came on Soft — his seven Good-ground runs show 1W4P from 14 attempts and his best trip has been 16-18f; JJ Slevin takes the ride and the horse races prominently with turf headgear, though the step to 2m6f on Good is a slight query after 148 days off.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: 185 days off and ran 14th on his only run over 18f on Heavy for Ross O'Sullivan; no jockey listed which is a concern in a 21-runner field, fades in the finish, and the form offers nothing to suggest he can be competitive off this layoff.

races.paceDynamic: Jeroboam Machin is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and, crucially, is unlikely to face any serious pressure for the lead on this Good ground over 2m6f at Galway — he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop that plays entirely to his stamina strengths. Behind him, Al Arrivee and De Jour En Jour are the most credible prominent racers, with Shoda and Frankie's Freebie also likely to press for a position in the first half of the field. The field carries more hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the true rear — Killowen House and Mr Erwitt are genuine hold-up types who, in a 21-runner maiden hurdle, are likely to find themselves racing closer to midfield than their natural style dictates, which dilutes their chance in a scenario that demands a late run from off the pace. The dominant race shape here favours prominent and mid-prominent racers who can track Jeroboam Machin's sustainable lead without expending energy early, staying close enough to pounce at the final flight — patient hold-up horses face a stiffer task with a predictable, measured tempo unlikely to create the bunching and gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jeroboam Machin sets a steady, uncontested gallop and prominent trackers have enough fuel to attack at the last.
scenarios.body: Jeroboam Machin rolls along at his own pace without a rival to pressurise him, and the horses immediately behind him — Al Arrivee, De Jour En Jour, Shoda — get a perfect tow into contention; the winner comes from the group travelling just off the lead turning in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Drifts, Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the steady gallop is so uncontested that Jeroboam Machin conserves enough to hold on, and the field strings out leaving chasers flat-footed.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to commit early, the tempo is so moderate that Jeroboam Machin essentially steals the race by default, and by the time trackers realise the threat he has stolen three lengths on them at the top of the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves faster than expected — perhaps Jeroboam Machin is pushed wider than ideal — and the race compresses late, allowing midfield stalkers to swoop.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace raises the tempo enough to compromise the front two or three, creating a bunched turning moment that benefits horses like Mr Hollywood or Killowen House travelling smoothly through the field; the Galway straight rewards momentum-building horses with stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Surge, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the field splits or there is significant interference at hurdles, leaving a hold-up type to weave through on the run-in.
scenarios.body: In a chaotic 21-runner maiden the risk of traffic incidents is real, and a horse like Mr Hollywood or Rumi Rock who jumps cleanly and finds a gap late could profit from the carnage ahead; this scenario relies on fortune as much as ability.

watchPoints.text: Al Arrivee (W P Mullins/Mr P W Mullins) has won twice on Good ground from prominent positions and arrives fresh — if he travels smoothly behind Jeroboam Machin's uncontested lead the combination of yard form and racing style makes him the primary danger.

Jeroboam Machin is the lone confirmed front-runner but is tagged STYLE_FIT — his best form came over shorter trips on Soft ground, and if he runs out of stamina approaching the final two hurdles the entire race shape could collapse dramatically.

Mr Hollywood (W P Mullins/Brian Hayes) has shown genuine class form at shorter trips and is likely to be produced late off the steady gallop — watch for him making eye-catching headway from midfield turning in, as this is precisely the scenario where a strong yard hold-up type can ambush the field.

Killowen House and Mr Erwitt are both true hold-up horses who will likely be forced closer to midfield than ideal given field size — if they do find themselves hemmed in or short of room in a 21-runner pack over the early hurdles, their chance of producing a late run diminishes sharply.

De Jour En Jour has placed on Good ground over similar trips three times without winning — watch for whether Keith Donoghue elects to press Jeroboam Machin or sit second; if he applies any pressure the tempo changes and the entire race shape pivots away from Scenario A.

runners_data.name: Hees Dynamite
runners_data.note: Sole genuine front-runner; gets to dictate entirely unchallenged, which suits its 5-1-1-P-2 recent form; 12 days since last run is fine, Good going suits (10/15 sim-going record), and the 8yo has winning form over this course and trip — the question is whether its OR=112 is enough to hold off all challengers from the front.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, with wins three and four starts back, but he's only 18th of 23 on our rating; he has raced over today's trip and going before, 12 days after his latest run.

runners_data.name: Harbour Highway
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for Emmet Mullins (1/7 in 14 days), a significant booking; hold-up horse with 1W4P on similar going and placed form over this trip — tongue-tie fitted, 29 days off, and the combination of Cobden and Mullins at Galway gives this a leading profile in the closers' scenario.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up placings in his last five starts underline the ability, and fifth of 23 on our rating is more than enough claim, even with a below-par effort when pulled up last time out; he has also raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer with a strong 3W5P record on comparable going (12/15); visor retained, 15 days since last run, but recent form 15P-47 is mixed and the OR=110 suggests it is competitive enough — needs to get a clear run from its prominent pitch in a 23-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, fourth two starts back, but a winner five starts back, and a rating of 109 puts him 12th of 23; he has raced over today's trip and going before, 15 days after his latest run.

runners_data.name: Oneforgonzo
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent type on a decent retrieval run (form 254-15), won over 20f on Good; pads headgear fitted, 7lb claimer Anna McGuinness takes off valuable weight — 69 days off is a query but OR=110 and proven Good-ground form over similar trips makes this a credible each-way prospect.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out but a winner two starts back, this gelding is workmanlike rather than progressive at 17th of 23 on our rating, and a 69-day absence adds to the doubts; he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Granville Street
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form over shorter trips (12-16f) raises doubts about staying 2m6f; best form on Good ground (2W3P at 6/15), but a sequence of below-par efforts at this trip level suggests the distance may be stretching it here.
runners_data.comment: Yet to feature at the finish in his last four starts, but a rating of 110 for ninth of 23 suggests capable form is still there; he has raced over today's going before following a 33-day break.

runners_data.name: Ollie La Ba Ba
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Good-ground winning form (2W4P, 11/15 sim-going); tongue-tie on, 51 days off — best effort at 18f so the extra yardage of 2m6f is a slight query, though the course form reads as solid enough to place.
runners_data.comment: Four sixths bookending a win four starts back make the form hard to fathom, though a rating of 111 for eighth of 23 keeps him competitive; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 51 days off.

runners_data.name: Camino Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a concerning recent sequence (99PPU) predominantly on Heavy; 188 days off is a serious flag, and the sim-going record on Good is thin — Rian Lane (7lb claim) does not offset the fitness and form questions for a 9yo back from a long absence.
runners_data.comment: Highly regarded on our figures, this gelding ranks third of 23 with a rating of 115, but the recent form is concerning - unseated, pulled up twice and two ninths in his last five - and he returns from a 188-day absence.

runners_data.name: Coded Welder
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a tidy record (4/20f GOO, 2/19f GOO) on Good; tongue-tie applied, 54 days off, and 0W5P in sim going — consistent but has not yet converted that consistency into a win on this surface and may struggle to get the full 2m6f.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, and runner-up two starts back, this gelding has been competitive without getting his head in front, and a rating of 115 for fourth of 23 rates him highly; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 54 days off.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's 6yo has sharp recent form — won over 20f on Good just 5 days ago, which is a very quick turnaround; hold-up horse (1W1P on similar going overall) with blinkers and tongue-tie, and T14 strike rate of 3/13 underlines current trainer form — the quick reappearance is the only risk.
runners_data.comment: A win last time out is the standout, but modest efforts before that - fourth, sixth, ninth and sixth in the four runs prior - explain a rating of just 108 for 14th of 23; he has raced over today's going before, quick to reappear just five days on.

runners_data.name: I'll Be Handy
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type flagged as fading in finishes — a significant concern over 2m6f; 0W0P on Good in five runs, 68 days off, and its best form has come on softer surfaces, making the combination of trip, going, and finishing tendency a marked negative here.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts three and four starts back show ability, but an eighth last time out and a rating of just 105 for 20th of 23 make this a hard sell; he has raced over today's going before but is 68 days removed from that last run.

runners_data.name: Lord Ffrench
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 1W2P on Good, 52 days off; placed headgear fitted, but a sequence of 6th, 8th, 6th, 7th, 7th in recent runs suggests it finds winning hard — Philip Enright takes the ride but the pattern of near-miss finishes is hard to ignore over this trip.
runners_data.comment: A win five starts back is now some way behind a run of modest finishes since, and a rating of 106 for 19th of 23 reflects that decline; he has raced over today's going before after a 52-day break.

runners_data.name: Imarajan
runners_data.note: Progressive 5yo prominent racer; won over 18f on Good 19 days ago and was placed at 19f on Good — 1W5P on similar going (9/13) shows strong ground suitability; tongue-tie and pads on, and T14 1/5 for Eoin Doyle indicates live trainer form — handles the step up to 2m6f as the key question.
runners_data.comment: A win last time out, and a runner-up spot two starts back, mark this out as in-form, though a rating of just 104 leaves him 21st of 23 here; he has raced over today's going before, 19 days on from that latest win.

runners_data.name: Andys Flame
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner who has been pushed back to midfield on the map as the field is overloaded with prominent types — likely to attempt to push forward in running; 9yo, 5 days since last run, recent form modest (/4-603), and STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 means its chance is materially discounted if it cannot get its preferred pitch.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, this gelding looks capable of running well again on a rating of 116 that puts him second of 23, though he returns for a yard currently winless with its last 24 runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: True prominent racer — winning form over 26f on Good (3W4P, 8/15 sim-going), and 2nd at 26f Good most recently — mapped to midfield purely by redistribution; most likely of the displaced front types to actually push forward and race near Hees Dynamite; 7lb claimer Alan King takes the ride, trainer has no recent form (T14: 0/0).
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out is a step forward, though a fall three starts back and a rating of just 104 for 22nd of 23 temper the enthusiasm; a winner four starts back, and he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with placed form at this trip on Good (3/24f GOO) for Darragh O'Keeffe; recent form includes a 3rd and a P, 23 days off — pads headgear, and the 1W4P on similar going over 24f gives some staying confidence, though the 000 run sequence before is a clear caution.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out is the highlight of a modest recent sequence, and a rating of 110 for 10th of 23 rates him more highly than the bare form suggests; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 23 days off.

runners_data.name: Tangara Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 125 days off — last won over 19f on Soft and has very limited Good-going form (1/5 sim-going, 0W); Peter Fahey's runner carries unknowns around fitness and the switch to a faster surface after wins on easier ground is a notable concern.
runners_data.comment: A win last time out catches the eye, but that was 125 days ago and a rating of just 104 leaves her bottom of the 23 here; she has raced over today's going before but the layoff is a concern.

runners_data.name: Lucy Wang
runners_data.note: A naturally prominent racer displaced into midfield by sheer weight of front types — 114 days off for Emmet Mullins adds a fitness query; 0W1P on Good going in applicable runs, recent form tailed off, and the redistribution means it is unlikely to get the pitch it needs, compounding the already difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out continues a consistent record that also includes wins two and five starts back, and a rating of 108 for 16th of 23 looks fair; she has raced over today's going before, despite having been off the track for 114 days.

runners_data.name: Mighty Berkshire
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for amateur Mr D L Queally (trainer-rider combination); 59 days off, 0W1P on Good, and a sequence of placed efforts at 19-25f — consistent enough but not a natural winner on this evidence, and the amateur ride in a 23-runner field adds a tactical layer of difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out is respectable enough, and a rating of 111 for seventh of 23 marks him out as better than his official mark suggests; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 59 days off.

runners_data.name: Therellbguddaysyet
runners_data.note: A 10yo genuine prominent type forced to map to midfield — 29 days off, recent form /4-58P is not encouraging, and the STYLE_FIT flag confirms its chance is heavily discounted when it cannot get its natural position; Good going suits historically but the age and form trend are concerns.
runners_data.comment: He sits highest of the 23 runners on our figures, a rating of 118 that puts him narrowly ahead, though pulled up last time out and modest form before that - eighth, fifth and fourth - are the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Macshadow Des Crai
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride on this 4yo hold-up horse returning from 122 days; predominantly soft-ground form (0W sim-going on Good), and the big-name jockey is the main positive — a long break and untested Good-ground profile make this hard to recommend at this stage of its career.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up two starts back is the standout form, though a seventh last time out and a lengthy 122-day absence temper things; a rating of 109 for 13th of 23 rates him fairly, and he has raced over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Clonbury Bridge
runners_data.note: A 10yo genuine prominent racer mapped to midfield; tongue-tie and visor on (hg: tv), 65 days off — best form over 20-24f on Good (1W2P, 13/15 sim-going which is the strongest ground-compatibility figure in the field), but age and redistribution mean it cannot count on getting its preferred early position.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up four starts back shows the ability, but two efforts pulled up in his last five starts and a 65-day absence are the concerns; a rating of 112 for sixth of 23 keeps faith, and he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Priory Park
runners_data.note: Another natural prominent type unable to get its position in this congested field; 102 days off, recent form 504P9, and a 10yo returning from a break — no jockey listed in data, which is a further negative flag in a competitive 23-runner handicap.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence, capped by a ninth last time out, offers little encouragement, though a rating of 108 for 15th of 23 is fair; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 102 days off.

runners_data.name: Mavetherave
runners_data.note: A 6yo prominent racer displaced into midfield; 0W2P on Good (4/9 sim-going), 25 days off, recent form 2050-8 — no trainer strike rate in last 14 days and the redistribution away from its natural position makes a winning performance
runners_data.comment: Runner-up five starts back shows some ability, but an eighth last time out and a moderate run of finishes since keep him hovering at 11th of 23 on our rating; he has raced over today's trip and going before, 25 days after that latest run.

races.paceDynamic: Hees Dynamite is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine rival to push it off its stride — the pace will be controlled and honest rather than frenetic, set by one horse dictating on its own terms over 2m6f on Good ground at Galway. The field is unusually front-runner heavy: Cornmarket, Andys Flame, Therellbguddaysyet, Lucy Wang, Clonbury Bridge, Priory Park, and Mavetherave are all genuine prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because they cannot all secure their natural position in a 23-runner field — of these, Cornmarket and Andys Flame are most likely to actually push forward and race closer to Hees Dynamite, though neither is expected to seriously disturb the leader's rhythm. The result is a race that will be run at a sustainable, metronomic gallop with one horse in control and a dense pack of horses forced to race out of their preferred position behind, creating a compressed mid-race shape that will decompress in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven class over this trip on Good ground and genuine staying ability — horses that can sit off the tempo, travel sweetly through the pack, and pick off the front-runner as the pace inevitably relents on the run-in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hees Dynamite Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Hees Dynamite bowls along uncontested and no rival has the will or position to land a telling blow before the last.
scenarios.body: Hees Dynamite dictates every yard of the race, sitting on a manageable gallop and kicking again from the second-last, turning its prominent role into a solo front-running performance with no one fresh enough to reel it in; horses that race prominently and stay well on Good ground are best placed to harry it home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner's lone lead creates a false pace that allows well-positioned hold-up horses to coast into contention and overhaul Hees Dynamite late.
scenarios.body: A controlled gallop means horse-power is conserved by mid-race closer types and they are fresh enough to rattle home over the final half-mile; hold-up horses with strong form on Good ground and proven stamina over this trip are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Disruptors Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Cornmarket or Andys Flame manages to push forward and force a genuine pace duel that creates a more pressured race, exhausting the leader and setting up a well-timed prominent finisher.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would string out the field, filtering out the hold-up horses that struggle to find momentum in a truly-run race; prominently-drawn types with strong course-and-distance form and good Going profiles would be the ones to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too slow, traffic builds behind the mid-race cluster, and the closers are trapped or run out of room in the straight.
scenarios.body: Horses shuffled back into midfield by the compressed shape find themselves unable to produce a run in a turning Galway straight with 23 runners; the winner comes from the front or just off it, with prominent types who tracked the leader in clear air proving decisive.

races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: She's A Fine Wine
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and key pace influence; won twice at Galway over similar Good ground and steps back here after a 45-day break off a Cheltenham win, but at OR=125 with top weight, the question is whether she can dictate and still find enough late up the hill in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and again two starts back, She's A Fine Wine brings the stronger form into this line-up and has run over today's trip and going before; a below-par ninth three starts back is the only blot.

runners_data.name: Venusienne
runners_data.note: Mullins and Cobden is a powerful combination; won on Good going and finished third at Grade level, suggesting class to match; a natural prominent type who should comfortably secure a front-rank position in this field and is the chief early threat to She's A Fine Wine.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner two starts back, Venusienne rates the biggest threat to top spot and has run over today's trip before; a below-par effort when pulled up three starts back is the risk attached.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton
runners_data.note: Won twice on Soft ground and her single Good-ground run produced only an 11th, which is a going flag worth noting; Dempsey yard quiet over the 14-day window; a genuine prominent runner who should find a position but may be vulnerable if the underfoot conditions don't ease.
runners_data.comment: Below-par when unplaced last time out, though the formbook shows back-to-back wins three and four starts back for Missus Beeton, who has run over today's trip and going before; needs to rediscover that better form.

runners_data.name: Billie Frechette
runners_data.note: Noel Meade runner who has placed twice over 2m+ on Good at Galway, giving her solid course-and-distance claims; naturally prominent and has the hurdle form to sit just off the pace, though she was beaten at shorter on Standard recently suggesting this trip is the minimum she wants.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and runner-up three and four starts back, Billie Frechette also won five starts back and has run over today's trip and going before; the main risk is the 59-day gap since that run.

runners_data.name: Samba Train
runners_data.note: Three wins from seven on Good ground including over 2m6f, so stamina and going are confirmed; a genuine prominent runner who regularly secures an early position; has top weight for age (5) to consider but Bolger's mares have run well at this festival.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and twice more in the past five starts, Samba Train boasts a strong scoring record and has run over today's trip and going before; question marks remain after a 79-day absence and finishes as low as sixth in between.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy a significant booking for Gordon Elliott; won on Good ground over 2m4f and placed at Grade level, arriving 25 days fresh; naturally prominent and with an elite jockey should slot into an ideal tracking position just behind the leader — one of the most attractively positioned runners tactically.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but rates towards the bottom of this field on our figures, and a fall among her recent starts underlines the risk; has at least run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: A true hold-up performer whose recent Good-ground win came from off the pace; OR=113 is workable and the 7lb claimer Peter Smithers is the only concern; if the midfield bunches and he gets a clear run from the rear he is the most genuine late threat.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to end an otherwise workmanlike recent sequence, and has run over today's trip and going before, but Splashing Out steps back out after a 61-day absence which leaves a small query.

runners_data.name: Zahra Dodville
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old with only four hurdle runs, trained by James Owen whose yard has been busy; finished second on Good at Galway last time, giving direct course form; naturally runs prominently but with her unexposed profile she could outrun her odds if gaps appear in the sprint home.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and a winner three starts back, Zahra Dodville arrives with a trainer among the yard's in-form performers and has run over today's trip and going before; a 67-day gap since is the only slight worry.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: Returned a pull-up in her last two runs and hasn't raced for 114 days, making her form very difficult to assess; the single win came over 2m2f on Good, which is the right going, but the recent P-P run sequence demands significant caution.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in each of its past two starts, Camlin Park rates bottom of this field on our figures and joins a yard currently out of form; a win three starts back is the only bright spot, but a 114-day layoff adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: Fratas
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the ride for Joseph O'Brien; a genuine hold-up horse who stayed on into second over 2m at Galway on Good, giving clear course-and-distance evidence; form string shows consistency at placed level and he is one of the few authentic closers in the field.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last four starts, Fratas has been runner-up twice in that sequence and joins a trainer currently among the yard's in-form performers, having also run over today's trip and going before; consistency without going one better is the pattern to note.

runners_data.name: Wonderfulwonderful
runners_data.note: A young 4-year-old with limited hurdle experience who won on Good ground at a shorter trip; McConnell yard has multiple runners with Camlin Park; she will look for a prominent berth and the step up to 2m½f is untested, so trip stamina is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, though Wonderfulwonderful won three starts back and has run over today's trip and going before; a yard currently out of form is the main concern heading into this deep field.

runners_data.name: Crohan Lady
runners_data.note: Won on Soft and placed on Good at 2m4f, so the trip and decent ground are within range; she is a natural front-running type who will be squeezed back by the volume of prominent horses in a 23-runner field — her chance hinges on whether she can overcome that positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and a winner three starts back, Crohan Lady has run over today's trip and going before, though a well-beaten ninth and eighth further back temper the overall picture.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has placed at 2m on Good and won over 2m on Good previously; instinctively runs up with the pace but in this cavalry charge she is likely to find herself racing further back than she'd like, which tempers confidence despite the solid going profile.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, but Cleopatra's Needle won two starts back and was runner-up in the two starts before that, and has run over today's trip and going before; back after just an 18-day break.

runners_data.name: Hillhead Runner
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning over recent runs at 2m-2m3f on Good; naturally wants to be prominent but the redistribution in a 23-runner field is a genuine tactical problem, and recent form shows only a second at 2m2f without a win in the last five starts.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts, Hillhead Runner was fourth last time out, with a much stronger runner-up effort five starts back the highlight, and has run over today's trip and going before after a quick 19-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Two Pair
runners_data.note: Won over 2m1f on Good and has placed at this sort of trip; a prominent racer by nature who secured a win on this going last season, but in a field this size cannot guarantee her position, and the long 74-day break is a question mark.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time out, Two Pair does have a win two starts back and a runner-up effort further back in its favour, and has run over today's trip and going before; a 74-day gap since that below-par run adds to the questions.

runners_data.name: Simple Things
runners_data.note: The 4-year-old Dempsey runner who placed twice on Good over 2m4f-2m1f; wants to race prominently but a field with this many pace rivals will push her back; two consecutive seconds suggest she runs her race consistently but hasn't yet found a way to win.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts, Simple Things was fifth last time out after back-to-back runner-up efforts two and three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before; needs to find more after a 51-day break.

runners_data.name: Astelia
runners_data.note: Has finished second five times in her last visible runs — placing type who consistently gets competitive without winning; Good ground is confirmed fine; will be mapped to midfield in this traffic-heavy race which may paradoxically suit a horse that travels with the pack rather than dominating it.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win despite three consecutive runner-up efforts, the latest coming last time out, Astelia has run over today's trip and going before, though the profile is patchier further back with an unplaced run and a seventh in its two starts before that.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: The fades-in-finish flag is meaningful at 2m½f; placed on Good over 2m4f-2m6f which shows the trip is within range, but if she gets competitive at the second-last and empties close home, that pattern could repeat in a field of this size.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but runner-up last time out, Bossy Bird otherwise has a modest recent record with back-to-back eighths further back, and has run over today's trip and going before; hard to fancy from a rating well down the field.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who won last time out (15 days ago, sharp turnaround) over 2m2f on Good; the fades-in-finish flag is a concern at 2m½f, and the quick reappearance needs to be weighed against the fact he arrives in form.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, though Small Bucks otherwise has a mixed record including a pulled-up run five starts back, and rates modestly on our figures; has run over today's trip and going before after a swift 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Ran just one day ago — an exceptionally sharp reappearance — which is the dominant factor here; has placed multiple times on Good at Galway, giving legitimate course claims, but racing back so quickly over 2m½f in a 23-runner handicap is a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Unseated last time out, though the form before that reads more solidly with alternating runner-up efforts, and Sea Of Doubt has run over today's trip and going before; a rapid turnaround of just a day since that unseated run adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Emesteraye
runners_data.note: No jockey declared in the data, which is a watch point at this stage; placed twice on Good over 2m-2m1f; a hold-up performer who has been consistent without winning, and the trip extension to 2m½f on a stiff track asks a stamina question.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but third in both of its past two starts, Emesteraye has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 27-day break; needs to find extra to go one better having missed out further back.

runners_data.name: Tingarran Express
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose most recent win came over 2m on Good at a smaller track; a natural prominent-type who wants to be near the pace but in a 23-runner field faces the same congestion problem as many others; age and lower OR suggest a watching brief.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time out, though Tingarran Express was runner-up two starts back and won five starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before; needs to bounce back from that below-par recent effort after a 26-day break.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: Has placed repeatedly at 2m-2m3f on Good ground, giving a clear going and trip profile that fits; instinctively runs prominently but will be shuffled back in this cavalry charge — her consistent placed form nevertheless suggests she will grind into contention if gaps appear.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, You Make Me Smile has a modest recent record otherwise including a win four starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before; rates near the bottom of a large field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: She's A Fine Wine is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-strong field and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — she can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop from the front on Good ground over 2m½f without ever being pressured into burning out her rivals. Behind her, Venusienne, Missus Beeton, Billie Frechette, Samba Train, Ardeen Joy and Zahra Dodville are all natural prominent racers who will be fighting for the handful of positions immediately off the pace, compressing the field and creating a bunched, attritional contest through the middle stages. The sheer volume of prominent-types means Crohan Lady, Cleopatra's Needle, Simple Things, Hillhead Runner, Two Pair, Astelia, Bossy Bird, Sea Of Doubt, Tingarran Express and You Make Me Smile cannot all get their preferred early position and will be forced to race in a midfield that is deeper and more traffic-laden than their natural style demands. With one unhurried pace-setter and a controlled tempo on Good ground, this race shape heavily favours horses who can travel prominently with the leading group — those positioned just off She's A Fine Wine in the first four to six — and who possess the class and stamina to sustain their effort up the Galway hill; true hold-up horses from the rear will have ground to make up late with limited gaps to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent racer dominates
scenarios.trigger: If She's A Fine Wine controls an honest but unforced gallop and the race is won by a horse tracking her in the first three.
scenarios.body: She's A Fine Wine sets a comfortable pace that suits the horses immediately behind her, and when the tempo lifts jumping the last they are already travelling, needing only to hold their position to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Off-pace class tells late
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield creates sufficient interference that the superior-rated hold-up horses find a clear run approaching the final flight.
scenarios.body: Fratas or Splashing Out, genuine hold-up types, are able to thread through a field that has been tightly bunched by the pedestrian early fractions, arriving at the last with momentum on their side.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapse; stayer wins
scenarios.trigger: If She's A Fine Wine goes too slow early and a wall of prominent types quickens simultaneously jumping the second-last, causing a stamina shakeout.
scenarios.body: The false pace followed by a furious sprint suits the horse with the best staying credentials who lengthens away from rivals flattening out up the hill; Samba Train's hurdle wins over 2m on Good ground align well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider exploits chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the traffic among the compressed mid-pack is severe and an unexposed or lightly-handicapped runner finds daylight at the right moment.
scenarios.body: Zahra Dodville or Simple Things, both younger horses running off competitive marks, could benefit from gaps appearing in a congested field if ridden with patience through the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Doubt ran just one day ago — watch for signs of fatigue or jockey connections scratching her; if she runs she could compromise her own chance and interfere with others racing in the same part of the field.

The compression of 10+ natural prominent types behind a single front-runner creates high risk of crowding and interference at the early flights — watch Crohan Lady, Cleopatra's Needle and Hillhead Runner as the most likely to lose position and cause traffic for others.

Bossy Bird and Small Bucks both carry the fades-in-finish flag in a 2m½f stamina test on the Galway climb — if either gets competitive at the last, watch for them to stop quickly and potentially impede runners coming from behind.

Camlin Park's 114-day absence following two pull-ups is an immediate safety flag in a large field of hurdles; connections should be monitored at the pre-race inspection and she is a horse to track early in running in case she is not travelling.

She's A Fine Wine's Cheltenham prep followed by 45 days off means watch her in the parade ring — if she has come forward physically she sets the race up for those tracking her; if she looks light or edgy her control of the gallop may waver and the race opens up considerably.

runners_data.note: Has shown smart form on good ground at 2m and 2m½f but three of his last four runs came on soft, and this step up to 2m6½f on good ground is a new query; Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim on 162lbs is useful and De Bromhead's good recent strike rate keeps him in the picture.

runners_data.name: Jesse Evans

runners_data.name: Ol Man Dingle

races.paceDynamic: Three Card Brag is the confirmed front-runner and, with 25 runners in a Grade 3 handicap chase over 2m6½f on good ground, is likely to establish a clear lead from the outset without being seriously pressured for the early gallop. Behind him, a dense group of genuine prominent racers — Senecia, Funiculi Funicula, Will The Wise, Jesse Evans, Ol Man Dingle, Perceval Legallois, Gorgeous Tom, Nowwhatdoyouthink and Downmexicoway — will contest the front-rank positions, meaning the pace behind Three Card Brag will be competitive but not frantic; the overall tempo should be honest and sustainable rather than suicidal. The field contains significantly more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Nouvotic, Maxxum, King Alexander, Spread Boss Ted, Solitary Man, Ballygunner Castle, Barry Lyndon, Conyers Hill, Jalila Moriviere, Boston Rover and Ballybawn Belter are all true prominent racers who will be shuffled back into midfield against their instincts, creating a congested mid-section and making the race harder to run on the bridle from deep. A controlled, honest gallop set by one genuine front-runner with a prominent-travelling position just behind him is the most likely shape: this race strongly favours horses who can secure an early prominent berth, travel fluidly in the first four or five, and sustain their effort from the second-last fence, rather than horses who will be anchored in traffic mid-pack regardless of their natural preference.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Rail Grind
scenarios.trigger: If Three Card Brag sets a fair pace and the horses immediately behind him — Senecia, Jesse Evans, Will The Wise, Nowwhatdoyouthink — travel comfortably in the first five throughout.
scenarios.body: The honest, sustainable tempo on good ground suits a prominent traveller who jumps well, stays every yard of 2m6½f and sustains their effort from the third-last; the congested midfield group are never able to land a meaningful late challenge from their unfavourable positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Sticks
scenarios.trigger: If Three Card Brag travels supremely well through a gallop that turns out gentler than expected and his rivals fail to organise an effective challenge from off the pace.
scenarios.body: With a clean passage and a good jumping round, Three Card Brag simply never comes off the bridle and the chasing prominent pack spend too long burning energy trying to close ground after the second circuit begins; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim gives the horse a meaningful weight relief.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late-Closer Benefits From Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group collectively set a slightly stronger-than-expected gallop and begin to stop in the final quarter-mile, leaving the genuine hold-up types with ground to make.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Diamond, Reverend Hubert and King Of Kingsfield are true hold-up horses who will have been ridden patiently in the rear and are likely to be travelling with momentum when others are emptying on the climb to the last; Reverend Hubert in particular has been in excellent form on good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the sheer volume of horses over early fences causes interference, fallers or significant shuffling that scrambles the intended race shape and produces an untidy, bunched contest.
scenarios.body: Several of the redistributed prominent types — Nouvotic, Solitary Man, Barry Lyndon — find themselves uncomfortably placed but manage to thread through when the field spreads after half-way, making this an unpredictable lottery that could throw up an unexposed or lightly-raced winner.

races.paceDynamic: Sunny South West is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner maiden and, critically, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — with Nakassama, Hopes Are High, and several other prominent types unable to secure their natural position in this congested field, the pace will be set by one horse at a tempo Mr Derek O'Connor can fully control. That uncontested lead over 1m4f on Good ground at Galway — a track where a settled gallop from the front is a genuine tactical weapon — creates a race that will be run at a comfortable, even pace rather than a searching one. The numerous redistributed prominent types (Nakassama, Hopes Are High) will be trapped in midfield against their instincts, burning energy and unable to stride forward freely when it matters. This race shape heavily favours a horse who can sit handy in the first four or five and produce a sustained finish, or the front-runner themselves if the tempo is truly uncontested; pure hold-up horses arriving late face an awkward task if the pace is modest and the race doesn't set up for a strong late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sunny South West Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sunny South West leads unchallenged and Mr Derek O'Connor dictates an honest but not suicidal gallop, saving enough for the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Sunny South West has winning form at 1m4f on Good ground and has been placed in five of nine starts at similar conditions — an uncontested lead over this trip on this surface is a serious weapon. With no rival willing or able to press, the front-runner dictates the fractions and any challenger must produce something exceptional to reel them in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Types Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to set up a finish and a horse tracking Sunny South West in second or third produces the best turn of foot in the straight.
scenarios.body: The prominent types who do secure their natural position — Run For Mahler, Daddy Long Legs, Galileo Springs — are well-suited to sitting just off the pace and picking off a tiring leader in the final two furlongs. Daddy Long Legs in particular has strong Good-ground form and a record of closing prominently, making this the most likely alternative shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the field strings out enough to allow a genuine late run from the middle of the pack.
scenarios.body: Horses like Hopes Are High and Nakassama — both natural prominent types redistributed into midfield — would need the race to collapse in front of them, but their true style means they won't be switching off at the back and could thread through if gaps appear. Can Happen and Silas Marner represent truer midfield profiles who could benefit if the tempo genuinely quickens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to cause early attrition and genuine hold-up horses are delivered with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Believe Again, Home By The Sea, or It's Good To Talk to be produced late into a well-strung-out field, but all three carry fading-in-finish flags and none has demonstrated the finishing kick to compensate. The probability is low because the pace is unlikely to be fast enough to set up a pure staying closer, and the flagged fade tendency in these runners makes this the least dependable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Sunny South West is the sole confirmed pace-setter in a 21-runner field — if Mr Derek O'Connor slots into the lead unchallenged from barrier, the entire shape of this race follows; watch whether any of the redistributed prominent types (Nakassama, Hopes Are High) attempt to challenge for position early, as that is the only scenario that disrupts the controlled gallop.

Run For Mahler and Daddy Long Legs are the two highest-quality prominent types who can actually secure a position tracking Sunny South West — if either is seen travelling sweetly in second or third place passing the halfway mark, they become the most serious threats to the front-runner.

Nakassama and Hopes Are High are natural prominent types forced into midfield; watch for signs of traffic trouble or restlessness in the first half-mile as they attempt to recover their preferred position — energy burned there will be unavailable in the straight.

Galileo Springs has no listed jockey at time of analysis — any last-minute jockey booking or scratching should be monitored as it could alter the market assessment of a horse who otherwise fits the pace shape well.

Can Happen runs just two days after its last start with blinkers fitted — watch the paddock for any signs of freshness or stress that could indicate the quick turnaround has taken a physical toll before the race even begins.

runners_data.name: God Of Power

runners_data.name: Amenita
runners_data.note: Weld's filly won on her most recent outing over 8f on good and carries the yard's 3/11 T14 strike rate; she is a genuine front-runner by nature but with so many prominent horses in this field she is unlikely to get her preferred spot — discount her slightly for that positional squeeze rather than any form concern.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but well beaten before that, Amenita sits bottom of this field on our figures and has run over today's trip before, though a 58-day break since her last outing adds to the queries.

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Two wins from his last four attempts, including twice at 8f on good, and has a jockey booking that suits his needs; he is another who should get prominent without the redistribution difficulty that affects others, and his recent form is strong enough to make him relevant.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins last time out and two starts back headline a strong recent record for Johnny Soda, who also won five starts back and has run over today's trip and going before from draw 4; a seventh and fifth in between are the only blots.

runners_data.name: Krasimir

runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a consistent run never worse than third, Krasimir rates a big threat on our figures and has run over today's trip and going before from draw 3; stepping up to face this field's best is the risk attached.

runners_data.name: Monvoe

runners_data.name: Monoceros

runners_data.note: Consistent at 8f–10f on good without threatening to win recently (5/8f, 5/8f, 3/10f in last three going-matched runs); by instinct wants to race up with the pace but is mapped to midfield given the crowded prominent ranks — modest handicap mark (OR 77) is a small positive.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back fifths in its past two starts leave Golddream with work to do, though a win four starts back shows the ability is there, and it has run over today's trip and going before from draw 9; hard to trust on this evidence alone.

races.paceDynamic: Mayflower is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press her hard, she is likely to dictate from the front at a sustainable, controlled gallop over this 1m½f on good ground at Galway. Moonlit Sun, God Of Power, Kirkland Sioux and Johnny Soda will be prominent in behind but none of them is built to take the race to Mayflower early, meaning the pace will be honest rather than fierce. This race shape — a single leader controlling tempo with a clutch of prominent racers tracking — classically favours horses who can sit just off the pace, travel well into the straight and quicken; it does not favour hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to generate momentum, as the tempo is unlikely to be fast enough. The field is saturated with prominent-profile horses: Amenita, Krasimir, Monvoe, Time Bender, Minella Rockett and Golddream are all natural front or prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply no room for all of them to get their position — of those, Kirkland Sioux and Johnny Soda, both OR-higher and in form, are best placed to actually secure their natural berth close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mayflower Controls, Pressers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mayflower settles into an uncontested lead and the race is run at an even, moderate gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Mayflower sets a sustainable fractions-controlled tempo and the contest becomes a sprint from two furlongs out, favouring horses who have tracked close and can accelerate on a sound surface; Kirkland Sioux and Johnny Soda, both in fine recent form and comfortable on good going, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mayflower Fades, Closers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If Mayflower's absence from racing for 66 days leaves her short of peak fitness and she begins to empty inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A front-runner returning from a lengthy break who has gone too fast too soon can leave the door ajar for hold-up types to come through late; Monoceros and Loch Gamhna, sitting deepest in the field, would benefit most if the tempo collapses and there is a genuine sweep from the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble, Prominent Cavalry
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed prominent horses — Monvoe, Amenita, Krasimir — push forward aggressively from the start and create a contested, faster-than-expected gallop.
scenarios.body: A hot early pace on good ground at a mile and a half would stretch the field and reward those with the stamina and tactical versatility to sit mid-division and stay on powerfully; Monvoe and Krasimir, both consistent placers on good ground, have the profile to benefit if the pace honest up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Form Turnaround, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the race unfolds untidily and a longer-priced runner finds herself in the perfect pocket tracking the leader.
scenarios.body: In a race where so many natural front-runners are jostling for position, traffic and interference can open gaps for a horse who finds a clear passage at the right moment; Minella Rockett, stepping back from longer trips and with a course win at 16f on good, could hit the frame if the run materialises.

watchPoints.text: Kirkland Sioux has won twice at this course on good going in recent starts and arrives on just a 10-day turnaround for a yard firing at 19/68 over 14 days — watch for him tracking Mayflower closely and mounting a challenge from 2f out.
Mayflower's 66-day absence and unproven stamina at 1m½f make her a dual threat: if she ties up in the closing stages the race could open up dramatically for anything chasing her home.

With six horses — Amenita, Krasimir, Monvoe, Time Bender, Minella Rockett and Golddream — all natural prominent types compressed into midfield on the map, a scrimmage for early position over the first two furlongs is likely; watch for crossing, bumping or a horse getting completely shut out.

Johnny Soda has won twice in his last six starts but all his wins on this going have been over 8f — this 1m½f trip is a step into unknown territory and if he lacks stamina he may fade tamely having sat close to the pace.

Amenita (D K Weld, 3/11 T14) and Monvoe each won on their most recent starts, and if either manages to get closer to the pace than their redistribution suggests, they could outrun a quiet market position.

races.paceDynamic: Rock Of Ireland is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse willing to set the fractions, will dictate from the front in what shapes up as a truly-run but uncontested lead scenario over 2m½f on Good ground at Galway. Gaoth Chuil, Wackestone, Liam Swagger and Sign From Above are natural prominent types who will push forward and apply some early pressure, but Rock Of Ireland is unlikely to be headed for long stretches and can control the tempo. The field carries a significant volume of hold-up horses — Rakki, Wahraan, Ben Hur, Forlio, Harry's Legacy and Papagei are all true closers who are mapped into midfield purely because the rear of the race is overcrowded; they are unlikely to obtain their natural position and should not be assessed as genuine hold-up threats in this shape. With a single pace-setter operating at a sensible gallop on a flat course in Good conditions, the race shape strongly favours horses who travel prominently or just behind the early leader and have the stamina to grind out the 2m½f trip — hold-up horses racing out of role are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Of Ireland sets a sustainable pace and the prominent stalkers sit close enough to dominate the straight.
scenarios.body: Rock Of Ireland controls the tempo, and Gaoth Chuil, Wackestone or Liam Swagger track closely before hitting the front in the final two furlongs; the Good ground rewards those who save energy by travelling prominently rather than making up ground from the rear. Horses with strong prominent-style profiles and good stamina at this distance are ideally placed to pounce when the pace steadies.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Of Ireland steals enough of a lead early that its rivals cannot claw back the deficit in the straight.
scenarios.body: Rock Of Ireland, uncontested at the front, dictates every fraction and arrives at the final bend with enough in the tank to repel challengers; on Good ground at a flat course a well-positioned leader can suck the life out of a big field. Prominent horses who press too hard too soon will find nothing, while the leader racks up the furlongs unchallenged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweepers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to exhaust the front-runners and leave the door open for those tracking just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Should Gaoth Chuil or Liam Swagger push Rock Of Ireland into an overcooked gallop, the leaders could tie up in the straight, allowing midfield travellers to pick them off late; horses like Eastmore, Cock And Bull or Black Heather — who travel economically and have strong Good-ground records — would benefit most. This scenario is partly dependent on redistributed hold-up types getting closer than usual, which is plausible but not the base case.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tired Field
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong pace collapses the entire front group and genuine hold-up horses navigate the traffic from the rear.
scenarios.body: Given that the true hold-up horses (Rakki, Wahraan, Forlio, Harry's Legacy) are all racing out of role in a compressed midfield, this outcome requires both a fast pace and a clean passage for horses who can't get to the back — both are against the grain of the expected shape. Any late surge would most likely come from those mapped to midfield with hold-up credentials who somehow secure space in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Rock Of Ireland has been off 87 days and is the race's only genuine front-runner — if it is short of peak fitness, the entire pace structure collapses and the race opens up for prominent stalkers like Gaoth Chuil and Wackestone.

Gaoth Chuil has won twice in three recent runs on Good ground and travels prominently — watch whether Chris Hayes places it right behind Rock Of Ireland early, as that could be the decisive tactical move.

Eastmore has a remarkable Good-ground record (14/15 in the frame) and suits the prominent profile, but there is no jockey listed for this runner — any late rider change or market drift should be noted before the off.

The rear of the field is severely congested with hold-up types (Rakki, Wahraan, Forlio, Harry's Legacy, Papagei) all forced into midfield — if they bunch on the turn for home, interference is a genuine risk and the winner is likely to come from the front half of the field.
Louiescall has strong Good-ground form and a prominent style; watch its market move late as a unexposed five-year-old trained by David Harry Kelly who won two runs ago at this sort of distance.
